scope: Medical Center Complex, Pediatric Inpatient and Pediatric Emergency Department population, including the source-listed pediatric inpatient, critical-care, emergency, procedural, diagnostic, and hematology/oncology areas; patients seventeen (17) years of age or younger.
purpose: To provide guidance for administering intravenous (IV) medications to patients seventeen (17) years of age or younger, with allowance for adaptation in extenuating circumstances.

IVPB: 2 hours, rapid infusion over 1 hour per MP order Manually flush line before and after use with 20 mL NS. No other medications at same time in line. Temporarily discontinue or decrease infusion rate with infusion-related reactions. Titrate first 3 induction doses and any change in dose that is twice the previously given dose. - For 250 mL total volume, begin at 37.5mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 75 mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 113 mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 150 mL/hr until completion - For 500 mL total volume, begin at 75mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 150 mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 225 mL/hr for 15 minutes; increase to 300 mL/hr until completion Vital signs at baseline, 15 minutes after start, and at completion. Rapid infusion inclusion criteria: 4 previously tolerated standard length infusions; receiving maintenance dose infusions; 15kg or greater. If dose is doubled at any point, the first infusion of the higher dose must be titrated at a standard 2-hour length one time before resuming rapid infusions.

Intermittent (IVPB) potassium: *Max peripheral concentration: 0.1 mEq/mL *Standard central concentration: 0.2 mEq/mL *Max central concentration: 0.4 mEq/mL (for specific clinical situations only, eg. fluid restrictions) *The maximum single dose is 0.5 mEq/kg (max 20 mEq), given over at least 2 hours on general floors and at least 1 hour in critical care areas. • If administered centrally: each minibag may contain up to 20 mEq. • If given peripherally: each minibag may contain up to 10 mEq. *A potassium level should be rechecked following completion of every cumulative dose of 1 mEq/kg (max 40 mEq) prior to giving additional doses. Potassium levels should be obtained at least one (1) hour after infusion completion. *Clearly label the syringe/minibag and line "Potassium-Do Not Use”. *Continuous ECG required for all intermittent doses. *Once potassium bolus is complete, flush with NS at the same rate the bolus was given to clear the line. Continuous infusions containing potassium (excluding TPN/PPN): *Max peripheral concentration: 80 mEq/L. For >40 mEq/L, attending approval required, dose (mEq/kg/hr) must be written, and volume limit of the infusion pump cannot be set for >2 hrs. *Max central concentration: 100 mEq/L (general floors) and 150 mEq/L (critical care). For >80 mEq/L, attending approval required, dose (mEq/kg/hr) must be written, and volume limit of the infusion pump cannot be set for >2 hrs. *Maximum rates: 0.3 mEq/kg/hr (max 10 mEq/hr) for general floors. Critical care and continuous ECG required for rates >0.3 mEq/kg/hr, up to a max of 1 mEq/kg/hr (max 20 mEq/hr) for critical situations. *Monitoring: Urine output every 4 hours for patients receiving >0.3 mEq/kg/hr and hourly on patients receiving >0.5 mEq/kg/hr. Consult the attending physician to determine an appropriate urine output.

sourceAlerts: Pages 1 and 3: The scope prints Gastrointestinal Diagnostic Center as ‘GILDC’ while the Procedure definition prints ‘GIDC’; the Pediatric unit selector uses the full source name and preserves this abbreviation mismatch as an alert.
Page 2: The Responsibility paragraph prints ‘CRNA)Registered Nurse’ without intervening punctuation; the source wording is preserved.
Page 2: The Mini-bag Plus definition prints ‘admixutre’ rather than ‘admixture’; the source wording is preserved.

Pages 1 and 3: The policy alternates ‘Neonatal’/‘Neonate’ Intensive Care Unit, ‘Post Anesthesia’/‘Post Acute’ Care Unit, and ‘Pediatric IV Medication List’/‘IV Medication Administration Guide’; the app does not silently normalize these governed labels.
